## SigningBackend interface

Backend that can enroll and use signing keys entirely on its own side.

**Signature:**

```typescript
interface SigningBackend extends SecretBackend 
```
**Extends:** [SecretBackend](./vaultkeeper.secretbackend.md)

## Remarks

Signing keys are a distinct resource from secrets: a private key must never flow through [SecretBackend.store()](./vaultkeeper.secretbackend.store.md)<!-- -->/[SecretBackend.retrieve()](./vaultkeeper.secretbackend.retrieve.md) or a capability token's claims. A signing backend generates the keypair, exposes only the public half, and performs the signature itself — the private key never leaves the backend. This is what keeps a key out of any JWE claims token and lets a presence-per-use backend enforce its guarantee for signing.

Implementations must keep signing keys in a namespace that cannot collide with or be read as ordinary secrets.
